An occupation profile can show qualifications typically needed to enter the field, the kind of preparation demanded and common tasks, and it may report a pay estimate or a projection, which should be read with its own population, date and scope.
A prospective student can compare what employers expect at entry level in the job market with the expertise a degree or a training scheme is meant to develop.

A mismatch between course content and local labour needs may pose difficulties even when the qualification is valuable elsewhere, and it would be too strong to assert that the route with the highest median pay always offers the best work-life balance.
The chart helps frame questions that need more specific evidence about occupations, costs and personal opportunities.
